diagnostic_steps: 1. Retrieve code P0300. 2. Perform spark plug visual inspection and replace if needed. 3. Test coil resistance. 4. Check fuel pump operation.

diagnostic_steps: 1. Confirm code P0420. 2. Conduct O2 sensor voltage sweep test. 3. Inspect exhaust for leaks. 4. Perform temperature check across catalytic converter.

symptoms: Check engine light, occasional fuel odor
likely_causes: Loose fuel cap, cracked EVAP hose, faulty purge valve
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify code P0455. 2. Tighten or replace fuel cap. 3. Perform smoke test on EVAP lines. 4. Test purge valve operation.

likely_causes: Worn torque converter clutch, low transmission fluid, internal clutch wear
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check transmission fluid level and condition. 2. Scan for any transmission-specific codes. 3. Perform road test to note slip patterns. 4. Inspect torque converter if fluid is adequate.

symptoms: Vibration in pedal when braking, noise
likely_causes: Warped brake rotors, uneven pad wear
diagnostic_steps: 1. Visual inspection of rotor thickness and runout. 2. Measure rotor runout with dial indicator. 3. Check brake pad condition.

likely_causes: Parasitic draw from aftermarket accessories, faulty alternator diode, loose ground
diagnostic_steps: 1. Perform parasitic draw test with multimeter. 2. Inspect alternator output voltage. 3. Check battery terminals for corrosion.

issue_name: Uneven Tire Wear Due to Worn Control Arm Bushings
symptoms: Uneven tire wear, clunking noise over bumps
likely_causes: Aged rubber bushings, exposure to road salt
diagnostic_steps: 1. Inspect control arm bushings for cracks or looseness. 2. Check alignment angles. 3. Perform bounce test on each wheel.

diagnostic_steps: 1. Visual inspection of hoses for cracks or bulges. 2. Pressure test cooling system. 3. Check coolant level and refill if low.

diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan ABS system for codes. 2. Inspect sensor rings for debris. 3. Test sensor resistance with multimeter. 4. Check wiring harness for damage.

diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0700 and related sub‑codes. 2. Check transmission fluid level and condition. 3. Inspect TCM connectors for corrosion. 4. Perform TCM reflash or replacement as needed. 5. Clear codes and test drive.

symptoms: Squealing noise, longer stopping distance, brake pedal feel change
likely_causes: Normal wear, aggressive driving, low-quality pads
diagnostic_steps: 1. Visual inspection of front pad thickness (<3mm triggers replace). 2. Check brake rotors for scoring. 3. Measure rotor thickness. 4. Replace pads and resurface/replace rotors if needed. 5. Bed new pads.

symptoms: Heavy steering at low speeds, steering wheel vibration
likely_causes: Failing electric power steering motor, loose wiring, low battery voltage
diagnostic_steps: 1. Check battery voltage (>12.6V). 2. Scan for any EPS-related DTCs. 3. Inspect EPS motor connector and wiring for corrosion. 4. Perform motor resistance test. 5. Replace motor if out of spec.

symptoms: Rear sag, uneven rear tire wear, clunking noise over bumps
likely_causes: Leaf spring fatigue, broken eye bolts, overloaded vehicle
diagnostic_steps: 1. Measure rear ride height compared to spec. 2. Inspect leaf springs for cracks or sag. 3. Check eye bolts for looseness. 4. Replace damaged spring or bolts. 5. Re‑align rear wheels after repair.

symptoms: Temperature gauge rising, coolant boiling, fan not turning on
likely_causes: Failed fan motor, blown fuse, faulty coolant temperature sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Verify fan operation with engine at operating temperature. 2. Check fan fuse and relay. 3. Test coolant temperature sensor resistance. 4. Apply 12V directly to fan to confirm motor. 5. Replace faulty component.

symptoms: Speedometer stuck, erratic cruise control, transmission shift issues
likely_causes: Faulty VSS, damaged wiring, dirty sensor
diagnostic_steps: 1. Scan for P0500. 2. Locate VSS on transmission output shaft. 3. Measure sensor voltage while rotating wheel. 4. Inspect wiring harness for damage. 5. Replace VSS if out of spec and clear code.

symptoms: Check engine light, reduced fuel economy, possible sulfur smell
likely_causes: Failed catalytic converter, oxygen sensor malfunction, exhaust leak before sensor
diagnostic_steps:

2. Inspect downstream O2 sensor voltage (should be stable).
3. Check for exhaust leaks near the converter.
4. Perform a catalyst efficiency test with a scan tool.
5. Replace converter if efficiency below spec.

4. Test purge valve operation with a multimeter.

symptoms: Shift delays, transmission overheating warning, slipping gears
likely_causes: Clogged cooler, low fluid level, faulty temperature sensor
diagnostic_steps:
1. Check transmission fluid level and condition.
2. Scan for any transmission-related codes (e.g., P0700).
3. Inspect cooler lines for blockages or leaks.
4. Test transmission temperature sensor resistance.
5. Flush and replace fluid if dirty or low.

symptoms: Pulling to one side, uneven brake pad wear, brake pedal feels soft
likely_causes: Corroded caliper pins, seized piston, contaminated brake fluid
diagnostic_steps:
1. Observe wheel movement when applying brakes.
2. Remove wheel and inspect caliper slide pins for corrosion.
3. Check piston movement by removing caliper bolt.
4. Bleed brake system to remove any contaminated fluid.
5. Replace or rebuild caliper as needed.

symptoms: Window moves slowly or gets stuck, clicking noise
likely_causes: Broken cable, worn gear, failed motor
diagnostic_steps:
1. Activate window switch and listen for motor sound.
2. Remove door panel and inspect regulator for broken cables.
3. Test motor voltage with a multimeter while switch is engaged.
4. Replace regulator or motor as required.

symptoms: Nose dive during braking, uneven ride height, leaking fluid
likely_causes: Damaged strut seal, worn bearing, impact damage
diagnostic_steps:
1. Inspect struts for oil residue or spray on the shaft.
2. Check for sag by measuring ride height on both corners.
3. Perform bounce test to assess damping.
4. Replace strut assembly if leak is confirmed.

symptoms: Battery warning light, vehicle won't start after sitting, dim lights
likely_causes: Parasitic draw from aftermarket accessories, bad alternator diode, faulty relay
diagnostic_steps:
1. Measure resting current draw (<50 mA is normal).
2. Pull fuses one at a time to isolate source.
3. Inspect aftermarket devices for proper wiring.
4. Test alternator output voltage.
5. Repair or replace offending component.

symptoms: Clunking over bumps, uneven ride height, leaking fluid on wheel well
likely_causes: Damaged strut seal, worn rod, corrosion
diagnostic_steps:
1. Inspect strut for oil residue or drops.
2. Check for play in the strut mount.
3. Perform bounce test for excessive movement.
4. Disassemble strut to inspect seal.
5. Replace strut if seal is compromised.

symptoms: Engine overheating, coolant temperature spikes, warning light
likely_causes: Thermostat failure, debris in thermostat housing
diagnostic_steps:
1. Observe coolant temperature gauge after warm-up.
2. Feel radiator outlet for cold flow; if hot, thermostat likely stuck.
3. Remove thermostat and test in boiling water (opens at 195°F).
4. Replace thermostat if it does not open.
5. Flush cooling system and refill.
